Key Research Thinking Patterns: Pattern 1: Homological Stability Approach (The researcher employs homological stability theorems to study the cohomology of arithmetic groups and their congruence subgroups, providing insights into arithmetic statistics and the distribution of central values of L-functions.)

Pattern 2: Koszul Property Analysis (The researcher investigates the Koszul property of the Steinberg monoid, defining a filtration on the reduced bar complex and showing that the homology of successive quotients vanishes in degrees less than n, with implications for algebraic topology research and mathematical proof verification.)

Pattern 3: Steinberg Module Resolution (The researcher constructs partial resolutions of the Steinberg module and uses them to study the cohomology of SL𝑛(ℤ) and congruence subgroups, providing lower bounds for the codimension-1 cohomology and vanishing results for the codimension-2 rational cohomology group.)

Pattern 4: Connectivity Conjecture (The researcher formulates and proves a connectivity conjecture for connected reductive groups over a field, generalizing the work of Ash-Putman-Sam on classical split groups, and refines known results about the first and second homology of SLn(Z) with Steinberg coefficients.)
Summary Description: Peter Patzt is a mathematician specializing in algebraic geometry, representation theory, and algebraic topology. His research focuses on the cohomology of arithmetic groups, congruence subgroups, and their connections to arithmetic statistics, analytic number theory, and algebraic geometry. He employs homological stability theorems, Koszul property analysis, Steinberg module resolutions, and connectivity conjectures to study these areas, with a focus on the Steinberg representation and its applications. His work has implications for algebraic topology research, mathematical proof verification, and the study of L-functions over function fields.
